ideas.title: Glassblowing at a beach furnace
ideas.critique: A viscous sheet whose stiffness climbs with cooling, glowing by its own temperature and ending as refracting glass, is physics and light the island has never had, and it shows off the tracer from start to finish. The danger is the plainest version: a mesh that scales and morphs along a script while colours fade, plus one more place with a furnace. Then the 'no two alike' promise is empty, and the shelf caustics are only worth it if the shapes really come out crooked.

ideas.title: A hot-air balloon on the island's own sea breeze
ideas.critique: This is the round-1 balloon again, but the scripted layers are now replaced by a solved sea-breeze cell that follows the time of day. That is a real step, and other things can use the wind field too. A single vertical slice means the wind is only real along one line across the island, and a slow drift still risks a dull film unless the turnover of the cell is made visible.

ideas.title: Sailing: tack against the wind to the islet
ideas.critique: Sail and keel as wings, with heel against righting moment and a capsize, give a strong control loop that players come back to, and a race against a best time works. But lift and drag on a lifting surface is the boomerang's physics again in a new hull, sailing is one of the most predictable vehicles a sea island could get, and 'the game's real wind' is only as real as whatever field sits under it.

ideas.title: A tightrope between the two pines
ideas.critique: A sagging verlet rope that bounces under the walker is a nice coupling, but the island has had ropes before, and a balance-beam game with A/D is a familiar minigame shape. An inverted pendulum on a moving support usually ends up tuned until it feels scripted, and the payoff, a fall and a splash, is the expected one.

ideas.title: Ants that find the shortest way
ideas.critique: Stigmergy on a GPU pheromone field is real emergent behaviour: the trail re-routes on its own, nobody scripts it, and it is the first swarm on the island that solves something. Ants are tiny and the earlier specks-on-grass takes read as dots, so if the trail cannot be read in the film it becomes the fireflies again, and the play is mostly watching after each crumb or stick.

ideas.title: A bottle organ tuned with water
same_form: The island answers a clap, a broken take
ideas.critique: Tuning by ear through a real cavity volume is a pleasing idea, and it is the first instrument the island has. But the Helmholtz pitch is one closed formula, so the depth rests on the pouring and the breathy synthesis. The film carries its change on the soundtrack and shows a static row of bottles, the same way the clap films did.
